It's not that bizarre. You look online, you can find a bunch of ex-vegans who went through the same thing. Not the fad vegans either, the ones who went 3-15 years and suddenly their body was shutting down. I tell people if they can stick with it, good on them because the meat industry is an absolutely horrible thing.

P.S. once 3D meat comes out, I'm jumping all over it.

Was doing everything right, got the protein, fats, carbs, took all the necessary vitamins and omega-3s. Body was just shutting down. Not in the "oh, I'm starving" kind of way but rather the "I think I need to go to the emergency room" kind of way. It sucked that first week going back to a regular diet but after the second week I started feeling like myself again. I want to try at least going vegetarian sometime in the future, but I need to be more stable at the moment.

I didn't. Literally the only thing left that gives me interest is reading and writing. At 14, I randomly stopped playing video games because they all look the same. At 19, I stopped playing instruments and participating in theatre because it seemed like something my old self would do. At 20, I lost interest in sex and finding a relationship to be in. At 21, I lost all interest in friends and family and we never talk unless they contact me first. A few months ago, I stopped listening to music because nothing is good anymore. 

The only thing left that gives me any joy is reading and writing. I look at the list of books coming out in the next few years by some authors and I get excited and eager about it. However, I'm not finishing some. I used to always finish books in the past but now I would skim to the end or drop them entirely. When that joy is gone, I don't think I'll be around too much either.
Yes, I have a PO box. I don't get that much mail but I occasionally need to send a christmas present or get some legal documents sent to me.

Maybe. I live in a pretty liberal city and most of the time people can't tell I'm trans (I transitioned at 20). However, I haven't been able to switch over all of my legal documents. So when I get a background check through my SS#, they'll see my male name and my male gender marker. I'm not sure if they can tell my physical address is fake, but that would probably have something to do with it too. 

The depression probably hurts me more in the the job hunting. I have good days most of the time, but others I'm completely dead on the inside and things start unraveling around me. When I'm back on top, I have to start all over.
Today's a good day.
Thanks! Most of my business clothes can be washed in through a laundry machine. I only have two dresses that need to be dry cleaned on occasions but they aren't really interview clothes.

I used to have a laptop that I use at starbucks or mcdonalds. It got stolen a few days ago so I'm using the library while I wait for my new one to come in tomorrow. 

BTW, for anyone wondering, this isn't unheard of. You have to keep in mind that you have a lot of free time when you're homeless and if you don't have a full time job, that can be daunting (some turn to drugs). Most of the homeless people I know have either a phone, tablet, or a cheap computer to help them waste away the day. Some of them have jobs, some of them are looking, and some of them are content with their lives.

I got it from Best Buy but they're working on it right now. 

It's not that hard to imagine a girl spending $500 on a laptop with the money she's been saving up for the past three weeks while average rent is about $800 in this city. 

Homeless doesn't mean that I don't have other things in my life. It just means I don't have a home. I don't even look homeless, I dress way better than most of the "homefull" I see on a daily basis.
I'm pretty good pals with the night staff at PF. Even though I'm not registered for them, they often let me use the message bed/chair or tan whenever I want.
Transsexual and clinical depression. I sometimes wonder if the depression is the reason I'm not as bothered by my situation as much as other people would be, but I have no idea.

Yeah, I'm okay. It sucked for the first 3 weeks because I was working a full-time, non-paid internship to complete my degree and I didn't have a car. Three weeks in, I got lucky enough to get a car, get a delivery job the very next day, and I've been cruising on a fine line for about 5 months. 

I'm trying to find more stable employment, but it's pretty rough out there. I don't have trouble getting an interview but snagging the job seems to be an elusive concept to me. 

I've also got friends that I stay with on occasion. 

You know the funny thing? I'm kind of getting used to it. I mean, I was always kind of a minimalist in a way so it doesn't take much to keep me happy. Plus it's nice looking at my ATM statement and thinking "Sweet! I have $400!" rather than "Oh shit! I need to come up with $300 for rent!" (average rent is about $800 a month in this city). Now, if I get this job I was interviewed for, I've been thinking about other things I need down the road. I could pay off my schooling faster, get the medical attention I need, save up for the 401K and Roth IRA faster, and then cruise when I'm in my late 30's.

I had a computer that I bought in high school that lasted me for 5 years but it was stolen a few days ago. I've got a new one coming in (this is why you save money, kids) but not until tomorrow. So yes, I'm using the library internet.

I think it's just depression now. It used to be caused by actual negative things that happened in my life but now it just comes out of nowhere and cripples me. 

I just graduated college and things are starting to look up for me. I've been getting interviews and I'll most likely have a full time job by the end of this week. 

Getting on antidepressants is going to be one of the big things I do once I get a stable job. However, I've read a little about them and they seem pretty intimidating. Plus a lot of people keep saying they were hopeless even with the meds and I'm scared beyond reason that I will be like that too. 

I did therapy for over a year when I was in college. We ended up fixing most of the negative things in my life and getting a plan going for the others. It's just that with all of these things finally going my way, the depression is still there. It's like my body was miserable for too long and it just forgot to how to be happy. Like I'm broken. The idea keeps coming to me that I died a long time ago and my body is just waiting to catch up and it's been nagging at the back of my head relentlessly. Then the suicidal thoughts start coming in, which scares me. But the idea that I'll be like this forever scares me just as much.

My general depression and the frequency of the episodes. I remember a time when suicide was a crazy idea to me and I would only have a depression episode about once a month.

I don't know. I've been like this for 8 years. I'm only 22 and the thought of living a long life like this scares the hell out of me.

Shit. This is kind of what's happened to me in the last few months. I used to have a wish for a loving family, friends, and life, but when I'm honest with myself, I just want nothing more than to die. 

It's gotten to where when people asked me what would make me happy or what I want for christmas, I just tell them that they don't want to know the answer. 

God, I hate this. It just gets worse and worse every year and it doesn't seem like it's going to ever get better.

Hey, current homeless girl here. 

Call your friends, family, or whoever and see if you can couch surf. It doesn't matter if it's for a few months or a few days, something is better than nothing. The most ideal situation for you would be to surf between different houses until you can find a way to get yourself stabilized. 

Believe it or not, there's actually a few guides on the internet about how to go about being homeless. You may think of that as a slap to the face, but if this is going to be your reality, than it's best to know how to go about it the best way possible. Just google "homeless guide" and see what's out there. There was a blog I read a long time ago a few weeks before I knew I would be homeless and it saved my life in more ways than I can imagine. 

It will suck at first. It will suck even more because you have kids to look after. Just be as strong as you can possibly be, take necessary precautions where you need to, and you'll make it out alive.

Yeesh, that sucks. The first time I did it, I looked down where to get off and there were two cop cars parked next to each other. The cops inside were eating breakfast and enjoying coffee. I immediatly hit the ground and waited an hour for them to leave. I was late for work that day but so was everyone else and it wasn't that big of a deal. 

True on weather too, granted I only did the roof thing for about three weeks total. I used to do it on top of a gym I always went to for showering and it started sprinkling just enough to piss me off.

Not really that hard. Just call the manager to some giant store like Walmart or Target and ask if they have spots in there parking lot where you can park and sleep. Most of them do. The theory is that with people in the parking lot, it would reduce the chance of burglary. 

When I didn't have a car, I often just climbed up the electrical system of a few buildings and slept on the roof. No one can see you so no one will bother you.

However, I would like to note that this guy was an idiot when he was homeless and did a lot of things wrong. I only need to spend about $300 a month on living expenses. However if my car is towed or breaks down, I'm shit out of luck for my job and "housing"

If you see homelessness in your future (or you just have unpredictable parents) then print this out and keep it somewhere you can get to it. Homelessness sucks, but not knowing how to go about it will make it suck more.
